summary: Explains the need for a new pair of IANA Diameter Command Codes for a vendor-specific application, the ITU-T Q.3303.3 Rw interface, which carries requests to authorize network quality-of-service resources and policy enforcement. This is an informational document.

eli5.summary: A phone company needs a way to ask permission to give a call good bandwidth. This memo asks for two new numbers to label those request and reply messages.

questions: diameter command codes for qos policy enforcement
how does diameter handle policy enforcement
what are the rw policy installation codes
subtitle: Diameter codes for quality-of-service policy enforcement

tldr.problem: The ITU-T Recommendation Q.3303.3 defines the Rw interface for authorizing quality-of-service resources and policy enforcement in telecommunications networks. This interface uses the Diameter protocol and requires new IANA-assigned command codes.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5431 registers a new Diameter Command Code (315 for Policy-Install-Request and Policy-Install-Answer), an Application Identifier (16777256), and AVP codes in the ITU-T vendor namespace. These codes extend the Diameter Base protocol for policy decisions about bandwidth, QoS class, and traffic flow processing.
tldr.outcome: The registered codes enable telecommunications operators to build policy enforcement systems that comply with ITU-T standards while using the standardized Diameter protocol, ensuring interoperability across vendor implementations.

today: RFC 5431 is an Informational RFC that registers Diameter codes used in ITU-T telecommunications standards. It remains in active use where operators deploy QoS policy enforcement systems based on the ITU-T Rw interface specification.

sections.title: Policy Decisions in Telecom Networks
sections.content:
The Diameter Base Protocol (RFC 3588) handles authorization and accounting across telecommunications networks. The ITU-T (International Telecommunication Union) added a new interface, the Rw interface, to handle policy enforcement for quality-of-service decisions. This interface sits between a Policy Decision Point (PDP, called a Policy Decision Functional Entity or PD-FE by ITU-T) and a Policy Enforcement Point (PEP, or Policy Enforcement Functional Entity or PE-FE).

The PDP decides what resources a user or flow should receive, and the PEP enforces those decisions on the network.
sections.eli5: In a phone network, one system decides if a call gets good bandwidth. Another system enforces that decision. The Rw interface is how they talk to each other.

sections.title: What the Rw Interface Carries
sections.content:
The Rw interface exchanges information about resource reservation and allocation, QoS handling (packet marking and policing), gate control (opening or closing paths for a flow), address mapping for Network Address Port Translation (NAPT) and Network Address Translation (NAT) traversal, and reports on how much of the reserved resources are being used.

The interface uses Diameter as its transport, extending it with a new command code and vendor-specific AVPs. This allows the system to coexist with other Diameter applications on the same infrastructure.
sections.eli5: The interface carries requests like "reserve bandwidth for this call" or "open the gate for this video flow," and reports on whether the network is actually using the bandwidth it reserved.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: RFC 5431 registers a vendor-specific Application Identifier (16777256) under the ITU-T vendor ID (11502), and a Command Code of 315 for the Policy-Install-Request (PIR) and Policy-Install-Answer (PIA) command pair. These codes distinguish policy enforcement traffic from other Diameter applications. Additional AVP codes (1010 through 1018) handle specific traffic and policy fields defined by ITU-T Recommendation Q.3303.3, such as traffic descriptors, burst sizes, and data rates.
sections.eli5: IANA assigns three permanent numbers: one for the application type, one for the command, and nine for the data fields the commands carry.
